title: Ctrl+Shift+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z redo is unreachable (contradictory key+shift check) — breaks keyboard redo, the only redo shortcut on macOS
description: The redo branch requires `mod && e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey && !isTyping`. In every real browser, holding Shift changes the printable key value, so pressing Shift+Z yields `e.key === "Z"` (uppercase), never `"z"`. Therefore the condition `e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey` can never be simultaneously true: when `shiftKey` is true the key is `"Z"`. The standard redo accelerator Ctrl+Shift+Z (Windows/Linux) and Cmd+Shift+Z (macOS) is dead. On macOS there is no Ctrl+Y fallback (line 60 only helps Windows users), so keyboard redo is completely non-functional for Mac users. The undo branch at line 49 (`e.key === "z" && !e.shiftKey`) works because Ctrl alone does not alter the character.
evidence: Line 49 undo: `if (mod && e.key === "z" && !e.shiftKey && !isTyping)`. Line 54 redo: `if (mod && e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey && !isTyping)`. Browser semantics: Shift+Z => KeyboardEvent.key === "Z". So line 54 is unreachable in real browsers; Cmd+Shift+Z on Mac matches NO handler (lines 49/54/60 all fail) => nothing happens, no preventDefault. The unit test (useKeyboardShortcuts.test.ts:67-70) fires `new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'z', shiftKey: true })` — an artificial combination browsers never emit — so it passes while masking the real-browser breakage.
